segments.2f0e364acd: Inc42, YourStory, Economic Times, Forbes India, Mint, Moneycontrol, Business Today, plus a developer-audience track for AI. Home-market exclusives, SEBI-aware framing and the ETHIndia, IndiaAI Summit and IBW press cycles, run from inside the region by one senior operator.
segments.bc18c140df: India Web3 and AI PR is run by Shilika Jain, a fractional senior operator working from inside the region, not a full-service agency. Three commercial models: an India Quarterly Retainer at 4,000 to 9,000 US dollars a month over three to six months, an India Single-Market Launch Sprint at 8,000 to 22,000 US dollars for one focused 14 to 21 day window, or an Always-On India Coordinator at 2,500 US dollars a month on a three-month minimum, with Indian KOL fees on top. The program itself is home-market-first: lead with an Indian exclusive in Inc42, YourStory, Economic Times, Forbes India, Mint or Moneycontrol, run the international tier-1 re-report 24 hours behind, keep SEBI-aware framing and the April 2026 crypto transaction-reporting obligations in the press copy, and add a developer-audience track for AI founders.

segments.064ad7de5b: <1>Funding has unfrozen</1>. Indian Web3 startups raised <2>$626 million in 2025 with $396 million in Series B and B+ rounds</2> per the Hashed Emergent India Web3 Landscape Report, a definitive break from the funding patterns of 2022 to 2024. The Indian business press is reading the category back with fresh eyes.
segments.fce3c1eab0: <1>The developer base is the deepest</1>. India's share of global Web3 developers rose to <2>15.2 percent</2> per Inc42, the fastest-growing developer ecosystem globally and the only major market trending upward. For an AI startup, that is the engineer-audience hook the Indian press wants in every founder profile.
segments.e1da289f3c: <1>India is the world's number-one adoption market</1> per the <2>Chainalysis Global Crypto Adoption Index</2>, with on-chain value received doubling year on year.
segments.a1341df633: <1>The regulatory frame is clarifying</1>. The Ministry of Finance is working on a consultation paper on crypto asset regulation, the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance is examining a coordinated legal framework, and Budget 2025 introduced transaction-level crypto reporting obligations from April 2026 ahead of the OECD's 2027 global standard. Indian press wants every Web3 announcement to confirm whether the new reporting obligation has been factored in.
segments.a0e6a744c2: <1>Finternet, the next evolution of India's Digital Public Infrastructure</1>, is expected to go live in 2026 with 30+ ecosystem partners spanning cross-border payments, decentralised identity, asset tokenisation and programmable finance. The press cycle for tokenisation, identity and payments stories in India is the most fertile it has been in three years.

segments.e6c3184eb7: The Indian dual-track that worked in practice
segments.a202966c01: The Bullieverse $4M seed in February 2022 was launched as an Economic Times exclusive, then run on two parallel press tracks. Mainstream Indian business and startup media (Inc42, YourStory, Business Today) carried a founder-and-funding-driven framing. Crypto-native outlets (NewsBTC, HackerNoon founder interview) carried tokenomics and gameplay detail. Each track was briefed off one fact sheet but with framing built for the audience, not adapted from a US template.
segments.b8a718dde0: The operational lesson generalises. In India in 2026, the home-market exclusive is the wave. The international tier-1 re-report rides on top of it 24 hours behind. Press cycles run in reverse of the Western default.
segments.434cdd4d9b: How a typical India launch unfolds
segments.a8c6c063b9: A 14 to 21 day Single-Market Launch Sprint for an India-anchored announcement:
segments.ff63fd9d43: <1>Days 1 to 4</1>. Pull the India-specific framing. Identify the right Indian outlet for the exclusive based on the audience that matters (Economic Times for mainstream business, Inc42 for startup ecosystem, Forbes India for founder profile, Mint for SEBI-adjacent). Draft the India press kit with the regulatory note (April 2026 transaction-reporting, MoF consultation status), the lead-investor framing and the India-developer or India-revenue hook.
segments.b6a7b12078: <1>Days 5 to 10</1>. Brief the Indian exclusive 5 days ahead under embargo. Brief the re-report destinations (the rest of the Indian press) 48 hours behind. Brief the international tier-1 re-report (CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, The Block, AI Magazine, TechCrunch) 24 hours behind the Indian exclusive lift. Brief 4 to 8 named Indian KOL voices for X, YouTube and Telegram coordinated activation.
segments.1105e05e73: <1>Days 11 to 16</1>. Indian exclusive lifts at 8 AM IST on a Tuesday or Wednesday. Indian re-reports follow inside the same day. International re-report lifts at 10 AM ET the next morning. KOL wave times to the international lift to give the Indian press 24 hours of clear air. Founder LinkedIn post and X-India post timed to the Indian exclusive.
segments.8bd3a73803: <1>Days 17 to 21</1>. Named Indian placements landed, audience overlap report, India-search-impressions delta, sentiment on the regulatory framing, and a renew-or-kill call per KOL on the wave.

segments.acb14b9eda: SEBI, RBI and the April 2026 reporting frame
segments.2b54790d37: Every Indian press announcement Shilika ships in 2026 carries an India-regulatory-aware framing line. The relevant frames:
segments.1469a7d34b: <1>April 2026 crypto transaction-level reporting obligations</1> per Budget 2025. Indian press wants confirmation that the announcing entity has factored the new reporting into its operations.
segments.3d328112cd: <1>The MoF consultation paper on crypto asset regulation</1> is the open question Indian press is tracking weekly. Press copy avoids framing that prejudges the consultation outcome.
segments.91b6b7e609: <1>SEBI's stance on token offerings</1>. Press copy never frames a token sale, IDO or listing as a securities offering in India. SEBI-adjacent framing means stating what the regulator has actually clarified, not what the founder hopes it will clarify.
segments.c98aae9c92: <1>RBI's stance on stablecoins and CBDC</1>. The Digital Rupee continues to operate in pilot. Press copy keeps stablecoin framing in the international context, not the Indian retail context.
segments.fd749900ed: <1>The DPDP Act</1> for any data-handling or identity-related announcement. AI founders in particular need DPDP-aware framing on training-data, inference, and user-data positioning.
segments.ccf9196f37: <1>Field note</1> Indian business press in 2026 wants to know whether the founder understands the April 2026 reporting obligation before they want to know the cap-table. The compliance line is the first paragraph, not the footnote.
segments.0e6a6542a3: The AI search layer for Indian audiences
segments.f135c92e5b: Indian audiences searching in English and Hindi see a mix of Google AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude responses on Web3 and AI category queries. Per <1>Google's AI optimization guide</1>, non-commodity content with named-expert bylines and strong E-E-A-T wins citations on these surfaces, and Indian press placements in Inc42, ET Tech, Mint and Moneycontrol carry exactly that signal. Per <2>Google's gen-AI content guidance</2>, originality, named expertise and substantive review are the bar regardless of language.
segments.74385ef7ae: The <1>Princeton GEO study (Aggarwal et al., arXiv:2311.09735)</1> found pages combining citations, statistics and named quotations get cited 30 to 40 percent more by generative engines, and the dynamic holds for India-English AI search too. A campaign that earns a named-byline placement in Inc42 or Economic Times, then re-reports across Mint and Forbes India, builds the citation graph that ChatGPT and Perplexity rank against on "best AI PR agency India", "Web3 PR India" and "crypto launch press India" queries.
segments.686886037c: Book a 30-minute teardown. We look at whether India is the right first push for the next 90 days based on your actual fact set, which Indian outlets map to your audience, the regulatory framing your press copy will need under the April 2026 reporting obligation, the event timing that should anchor the launch, the named Indian KOL voices that fit the brief, and which engagement shape (Quarterly Retainer, Single-Market Sprint or Always-On Coordinator) is the right one for your cycle. By the end of the call you will know whether the budget belongs in an India push this quarter or somewhere else entirely.
segments.227ef53cc5: What does an India Web3 or AI PR program actually cover?
segments.a91bc2ecc9: Seven workstreams. One: home-market exclusive lead with Inc42, YourStory, Economic Times, Forbes India, Mint or Moneycontrol depending on the audience. Two: Indian re-report wave across Business Today, Business Standard, The Hindu BusinessLine, NDTV Profit and CNBC TV18 timed to lift inside the same day as the exclusive. Three: tier-1 international re-report through CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, The Block, Decrypt, AI Magazine or TechCrunch 24 hours behind the Indian lift. Four: named Indian KOL voices on X, YouTube and Telegram with FTC-and-DPDP-aware briefs. Five: SEBI, RBI and MoF regulatory framing baked into every press copy under the April 2026 transaction-reporting obligation. Six: on-ground event leverage at ETHIndia, IBW, IndiaAI Summit and Global Fintech Fest. Seven: founder LinkedIn and X-India activation timed to the press cycle.
segments.592c3c0874: How much does India Web3 or AI PR cost in 2026?
segments.9be34a1dd3: Three commercial models. India Quarterly Retainer runs 4,000 to 9,000 US dollars per month over three to six months and covers one to two named-Indian placements per quarter plus the international re-report wave. India Single-Market Launch Sprint runs 8,000 to 22,000 US dollars total for one focused 14 to 21 day window timed to a launch, raise or event. Always-On India Coordinator runs 2,500 US dollars per month with a three-month minimum. Indian KOL fees sit on top. Published 2026 Indian KOL rates run nano 150 to 1,200 US dollars per deliverable, micro 400 to 4,000, mid 6,000 to 18,000, macro 12,000 to 40,000 plus, with the Indian premium concentrated on the X-and-YouTube combined-deliverable tier.
segments.000ab54891: Why does the Indian exclusive land before the international press?
segments.1bf4bcc6d9: Because the audience that converts on an Indian founding story is in India. The Indian business press treats a home-market exclusive as a signal that the founder understands the country, not a courtesy add-on. The international tier-1 cycle then re-reports on top of the Indian lift, which has the bonus effect that the international press is reading the Indian lead as third-party validation rather than the inverse. The Bullieverse 2022 seed and the Web3Auth and Coin DCX cycles all worked off this sequencing pattern.
segments.7131c2e14c: How does the April 2026 crypto transaction-reporting obligation change Indian press copy?
segments.57d32fa593: Every Web3 announcement now needs to confirm in the first three paragraphs that the announcing entity has factored the new reporting obligation into operations. Press copy that does not name the reporting obligation reads as either uninformed or evasive to Indian financial press. The compliance line moves from footnote to first paragraph. SEBI-adjacent framing remains the standard for any token-offering language, and the consultation paper from the Ministry of Finance is the open question Indian press is tracking weekly.
segments.a78e0441aa: Does India PR earn AI search citations on Indian English and Hindi queries?
segments.8f815d9347: Yes. Indian audiences searching in English and Hindi see a mix of Google AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude responses on Web3 and AI category queries. Named-byline placements in Inc42, ET Tech, Mint, Moneycontrol and Forbes India carry the named-expertise and E-E-A-T signal Google explicitly names in its AI optimization guide. The Princeton GEO study found pages combining citations, statistics and named quotations get cited 30 to 40 percent more by generative engines, and the dynamic holds for India-English AI search too.
segments.1631320db0: Which Indian outlets are the right exclusives for an AI startup versus a Web3 startup?
segments.eed400a488: For an AI startup with a developer-audience hook, Inc42 ET Tech or Forbes India for the founder profile and category narrative. For an AI startup with an enterprise-customer announcement, Economic Times and Business Today for the customer-name framing. For a Web3 startup launching a token or mainnet, Mint or Moneycontrol for the regulatory and market-impact framing. For a Web3 startup raising a Series A or B, Economic Times for the funding lead with Inc42 and YourStory as same-day re-reports. For a category-defining founder profile, Forbes India for the long-form arc. The 30-minute teardown call picks the right exclusive off the actual fact set.
segments.988d69d2b6: Does Shilika work with NRI and Indian-origin founders based outside India?
segments.2c4f3b40b3: Yes. The NRI and Indian-origin founder track is one of the highest-leverage shapes the practice runs. The Indian home-market exclusive plus the US or UK tier-1 re-report sequence works whether the founder is in Bengaluru, Mountain View, Singapore or Dubai. The framing simply puts the founder country-of-origin and the Indian engineer-or-customer footprint at the top of the brief rather than burying it in the bio.
